Repertoire statistics (SNG-13) — manual test

Date: 2026-11-16 · Branch: feature/repertoire-stats (stacked on #1106) · Tested on: the local Supabase stack on the Mac (StrummyLocal), admin account, Polish locale (?lang=pl) · Design: Claude Design project “Strummy”, file “Strummy - Statystyki repertuaru”.

What was done

The admin page /dashboard/admin/repertoire-stats rebuilt after the Claude Design board: six views, all state in the URL, a note-name switch (B/Bb ↔ H/B, ?names=pl) and a CSV export of every list (/api/admin/repertoire-stats/csv, admin only).

ViewWhat it answers
OverviewWhat is missing: coverage as steps on one 0–468 axis (analyses outnumber links: 52 come from a recording found elsewhere), the transcription target (~360), beats per bar, and the songs missing each step, the ones most students have in their repertoire first.
Strummy vs recordingWhere Strummy is wrong: errors to fix on a white card, explained disagreements muted below with their reason — guitar tuned down (chords agree after a −1 shift), another shift, capo, relative key, half/double tempo, unsure key detection. Chords show their scale degrees.
SongsEvery song with Strummy beside the recording (tempo, key, capo vs suggested capo, length, share of chords heard), filtered and sorted on the server, 50 per page; up to three songs side by side.
Song vs repertoireTempo, key, highest/lowest vocal note, bass density. Numbers as a percentile with named extremes (never 0%/100%); keys only as “same key as N songs”; under 30 songs a point per song and a count. Chart/Table switch on every card.
ProgressionsRanking of the recordings' progressions in degrees, known patterns (Pop, Axis, Blues, ii–V–I…), and one song's progressions against Strummy's chord sheet (or only its chord list: “order uncertain”), with the recording's sections.
ArrangementEvery transcribed track (11) of up to three songs A/B/C: share of bars playing, notes per bar, range against the transcribed repertoire.

Decisions where the design left a choice: funnel and table variant A; the board's “9 today / 360 target” toggle was a demo, the page switches to a histogram by itself at 30 songs; the capo song2logic suggests is a playing hint (it differs in 249 songs), shown in the table and comparison, never a disagreement; students = distinct students with the song in student_repertoire; the analysis knows beats per bar only (“4 per bar”, no 6/8 vs 3/4).

Also fixed on the way: the chords column of some songs holds tab lines and words (“Bend”, “Capo:”) the lenient parser read as chords; only real chord symbols count now.

How to test

  1. Start the local stack and the app on this branch; sign in as admin; open Analytics → Repertoire Stats.
  2. Overview: the four steps add up as above; each missing-data group lists songs, “Show the other N” unfolds the rest, CSV downloads that group.
  3. Strummy vs recording: filter Chords — Little Wing and American Idiot sit under “Explained” with “Tuned down a half step”; a tempo error reads “Different tempo (−30%)”.
  4. Songs: search, category pills, level, “Only with disagreements”, sort by a header; tick 2–3 songs — the comparison opens under the table; “Copy link” reproduces it.
  5. Song vs repertoire: pick a song by typing; with a transcription the vocal and bass cards show points and “k of n”; the key card says only how many songs share the key.
  6. Progressions: open a ranking row, pick a song from it; a song without a chord sheet shows the dashed “order uncertain” frame.
  7. Arrangement: remove a song (×), add another from the dashed list.
  8. Switch H/B: every chord, key and note renames (B → H, Bb → B). Try a phone width and dark mode.
